answer: With 10% down at the September 2026 average 30-year rate (6.862%), the original schedule brings the loan to 80% of the purchase price after 99 payments and to 78% after 114: about 8 to 9.5 years of mortgage insurance if home values are ignored. Measured against the national home-price index instead, buyers who put 10% down in 307 purchase months from January 1991 to July 2016 reached a loan of 80% of the index value after a median of 23 months; 14.7% needed more than 60 months, and October 2005 buyers needed 112. At the two-year mark, 58.6% of 403 purchase months (1991-2024) were at or below 80% of index value, but only 15.6% were at or below 75%. History, not a forecast.
guess: Buyers expect to pay mortgage insurance for most of a decade, until the loan is paid down to 80% of what they paid; price gains are rarely counted.
changesDecision: The years of insurance a 10%-down buyer is pricing in are usually the schedule's 8+ years; national price history says equity on paper often reached 80% in about two years, but not reliably (one in seven purchase months took over five years, and lender value-based rules are stricter). The viewer can compare the real range, not one number, with the extra years of renting needed to reach 20%.

assumptions: Loan = 90% of price, 30-year fixed at the monthly average survey rate of the purchase month, level payments, no extra principal.
Home value moves with the national purchase-only index from the purchase month; no individual-home or local variation.
Ignores closing costs, appraisal fees, insurance premium size, and lender seasoning or loan-to-value rules for removing insurance based on current value.
Index loan-to-value is a measure of equity on paper, not a statement that insurance would have been removed.
limits: History, not a forecast. A national index hides large local and individual differences. Removal based on current value is set by the lender or investor (appraisal, minimum seasoning, often 75% in early years), so the index result is an upper bound on how early removal was possible. The law-based schedule (80% request, 78% automatic) depends only on the original value.
